questions.question_text: You are preparing a dataset for machine learning and need to balance storage costs with performance. You have decided to use Amazon EBS General Purpose SSD (gp2) volumes for their cost-effectiveness while ensuring sufficient IOPS for your workload. Which two of the following actions should you take to optimize the performance of gp2 volumes? (Select TWO)
options: A. Enable EBS optimization on an EC2 instance to maximize throughput
B. Use Amazon S3 for storing large datasets and transfer them to gp2 volumes as needed
C. Configure gp2 volumes with high IOPS to ensure sufficient performance
D. Implement a caching layer using Amazon ElastiCache to reduce read requests to the gp2 volume
E. Optimize your EBS volume types by choosing Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) for critical workloads
questions.explanation:
A. ENABLE EBS OPTIMIZATION ON AN EC2 INSTANCE TO MAXIMIZE THROUGHPUT - Correct. Enabling EBS optimization on an EC2 instance can significantly increase the network throughput between the instance and its attached gp2 volumes, which is beneficial for performance-critical workloads.

B. USE AMAZON S3 FOR STORING LARGE DATASETS AND TRANSFER THEM TO GP2 VOLUMES AS NEEDED - Incorrect. While Amazon S3 is a cost-effective storage solution, it does not provide the same IOPS and throughput as gp2 volumes for on-demand access. It would be suboptimal to use S3 for storing large datasets that need frequent access.

C. CONFIGURE GP2 VOLUMES WITH HIGH IOPS TO ENSURE SUFFICIENT PERFORMANCE - Incorrect. General Purpose SSD (gp2) volumes are designed to provide a balance of IOPS and throughput, but they do not support configuring high IOPS as you would with Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1). Using gp2 for its intended purpose is the correct approach.

D. IMPLEMENT A CACHING LAYER USING AMAZON ELASTICACHE TO REDUCE READ REQUESTS TO THE GP2 VOLUME - Correct. Implementing a caching layer using Amazon ElastiCache can reduce read requests to the gp2 volume, thereby improving overall performance and reducing costs by offloading some of the workload from the EBS volumes.

E. OPTIMIZE YOUR EBS VOLUME TYPES BY CHOOSING PROVISIONED IOPS SSD (IO1) FOR CRITICAL WORKLOADS - Incorrect. While Provisioned IOPS SSD (io1) is suitable for critical workloads requiring high and predictable IOPS, it would be overkill and more expensive than gp2 volumes for the general-purpose workload described here.
